title: Cause and effect: reading for why things happen
subject: LITERACY

objectives.statement: Identify the cause and the effect in a short text, using signal words where they appear.

moe.note: MOE Grade 6 English: 'Analyze texts on varying topics'. Cause and effect is one analysis skill within it; proposed, not an MOE-named objective.

objectives.statement: Explain in writing how a cause leads to an effect in a text, including when no signal word is given, without claiming more than the text shows.

moe.note: Written explanation of implicit causes goes beyond 'analyze texts' and is LiberiaLearn mastery.

successCriteria.independentPerformance: Reading an unseen short text on their own, the learner writes a correct cause-and-effect pair the right way round in a full sentence with a linking word, and does so again one week later.

Without help, the learner writes a three-step chain from an unseen text using its evidence, states when a text only suggests a cause, and predicts plausible effects for an unfamiliar text type such as a school notice.

prerequisites: Can read a short grade-level paragraph and retell what happened in order.
Uses the words because and so correctly in everyday speech.

layers.nationalFoundation: Finding causes and effects in short texts as part of MOE Grade 6 text analysis.
layers.liberiaLearnMastery: Written explanation of causal chains, implicit causes and careful claims, with misconception-specific feedback and a 7-day retrieval.
layers.globalExcellence: Transfer to an unfamiliar genre (a school notice) by predicting effects, and an optional causal-chain story.

legacyDisposition.heading: 1. Hook — The Real-World Challenge
legacyDisposition.rationale: Fatu's stall story kept and shortened from 272 to about 70 words; 'make a killing' and the career framing removed.

legacyDisposition.heading: 2. Learning Objectives
legacyDisposition.rationale: Three objectives, one of them story writing that the lesson never teaches, replaced by two assessable reading objectives. Story writing moves to the next lesson and the optional extension.

legacyDisposition.heading: 3. Prior Knowledge Activation
legacyDisposition.rationale: The salty-food example is reused as a diagnostic item; answers were shown to learners and are now feedback after a choice.

legacyDisposition.heading: 4. Core Concept — Concrete Foundation
legacyDisposition.rationale: The flood example and the definitions are reused. Dropped the unsupported claim that cassava is planted 'only during dry seasons to avoid spoilage'. Reviewer to confirm.

legacyDisposition.heading: 5. Core Concept — The Rule and Why It Works
legacyDisposition.rationale: The rule that a cause 'will always lead to some effect' overgeneralizes; replaced by the 'always is too strong' check.

legacyDisposition.heading: 6. Key Vocabulary
legacyDisposition.rationale: Cause and effect definitions and the flooded-street example reused, condensed into key points.

legacyDisposition.heading: 7. Worked Example 1
legacyDisposition.rationale: The flood and cassava-price chain is kept as a short reading text. The invented figures (LD 200 to LD 400, 10 to 2 tons) are dropped because they were not labelled as invented.

legacyDisposition.heading: 8. Worked Example 2 — Alternative Method
legacyDisposition.rationale: The 'start from the effect' method is kept and applied to a text with no signal word.

legacyDisposition.heading: 9. Error Analysis
legacyDisposition.rationale: Error 3 (overgeneralization) is reused. Error 1's correction is wrong: more buyers can raise prices, so it was removed. Reviewer to confirm.

legacyDisposition.heading: 10. Guided Practice Problem 1
legacyDisposition.rationale: The legacy text teaches that playing in the rain caused Boima's cold. Colds are caused by viruses, so the example now teaches that 'after' is not 'because'. Reviewer to confirm.

legacyDisposition.heading: 11. Guided Practice Problem 2
legacyDisposition.rationale: Repeats Problem 3's pattern and showed its answers inline; Problem 3 is kept instead.

legacyDisposition.heading: 12. Guided Practice Problem 3
legacyDisposition.rationale: Boimah's stall reused as a reading text with items.

legacyDisposition.heading: 13. Independent Practice — Tier 1 Foundational
legacyDisposition.rationale: Zoe and Kollie problems reused; answers were printed next to the problems and are now feedback after a choice.

legacyDisposition.heading: 14. Independent Practice — Tier 2 Standard
legacyDisposition.rationale: Answers were printed with the problems; the time-management item is covered by the retention task.

legacyDisposition.heading: 15. Independent Practice — Tier 3 Advanced
legacyDisposition.rationale: The St. Paul River clean-up is reused without a signal word, to practise implicit causes; the river is no longer named, to avoid an unverified ecological claim.

legacyDisposition.heading: 16. Group Discussion and Cross-Curricular Connection
legacyDisposition.rationale: A useful optional class discussion; it does not produce individual evidence.

legacyDisposition.heading: 17. Assessment, Exit Ticket, and Lesson Summary
legacyDisposition.rationale: The personal-reflection exit questions cannot show the objective; replaced by unseen-text written tasks with rubrics.

openDecisions.question: The live lesson tells learners that playing in rain caused a cold. Should the class that used it receive a correction?
openDecisions.authorRecommendation: Yes, through the teacher, independent of whether this candidate is released.

openDecisions.question: The legacy lesson promised story writing. Accept moving it to the next lesson?
openDecisions.authorRecommendation: Accept; the extension keeps a non-gating path.
